plan.subject: LLM agents

queries.query: ("LLM agent" OR "language model agent" OR "large language model agent" OR "autonomous language agent")
queries.rationale: Catches the main body of work that explicitly identifies itself as LLM or language-model agent research.

queries.query: ("agentic AI" OR "agentic system" OR "agentic workflow" OR "agentic language model")
queries.rationale: Finds newer papers using the agentic AI vocabulary rather than the older LLM-agent phrasing.

queries.query: ("LLM" OR "language model" OR "large language model") AND (planning OR "task decomposition" OR "hierarchical planning" OR replanning)
queries.rationale: Targets work on how agents break down and sequence tasks, a core architectural concern for practical agent design.

queries.query: ("LLM" OR "language model" OR "large language model") AND ("tool use" OR "function calling" OR "API calling" OR "tool augmented")
queries.rationale: Captures agent papers centered on external action, APIs, and tool invocation rather than pure text interaction.

queries.query: ("LLM" OR "language model" OR "large language model") AND ("multi-agent" OR multiagent OR "society of agents" OR "agent collaboration")
queries.rationale: Finds architectures where multiple language-model agents coordinate, debate, or specialize.

queries.query: ("LLM" OR "language model" OR "large language model") AND (memory OR "long-term memory" OR "episodic memory" OR "agent memory")
queries.rationale: Covers persistent context, retrieval-backed memory, and state handling that materially affect agent behavior over time.

queries.query: ("LLM" OR "language model" OR "large language model") AND (reflection OR self-reflection OR critique OR self-correction)
queries.rationale: Targets agent techniques that use critique, reflection, or iterative correction to improve performance.

queries.query: ("LLM" OR "language model" OR "large language model") AND (reasoning OR deliberation OR "chain of thought" OR "tree of thoughts")
queries.rationale: Finds work on internal deliberation and inference strategies that often transfer directly into agent architectures.

queries.query: ("LLM" OR "language model" OR "large language model") AND ("web agent" OR "browser agent" OR "computer use" OR "GUI agent")
queries.rationale: Captures agents that act in browsers, desktops, or GUIs, which are especially relevant to real-world engineering workflows.

queries.query: ("LLM" OR "language model" OR "large language model") AND ("code agent" OR "software engineering agent" OR "program repair" OR "code generation")
queries.rationale: Targets agent work most directly relevant to a software engineer, including coding, debugging, and repository-scale tasks.

queries.query: ("LLM" OR "language model" OR "large language model") AND (benchmark OR evaluation OR AgentBench OR SWE-bench)
queries.rationale: Finds papers introducing or using agent benchmarks and evaluation setups that shape what techniques look practically useful.

queries.query: ("LLM" OR "language model" OR "large language model") AND (hallucination OR reliability OR robustness OR verification)
queries.rationale: Covers practical limitations and safeguards for agents operating in open-ended environments.

queries.query: ("LLM" OR "language model" OR "large language model") AND ("retrieval augmented generation" OR RAG OR retrieval)
queries.rationale: Captures agent designs that use retrieval or knowledge access as part of action and decision-making.

queries.query: ("LLM" OR "language model" OR "large language model") AND ("workflow automation" OR orchestration OR pipeline OR executor)
queries.rationale: Finds engineering-oriented work on chaining, orchestration, and execution patterns for agent systems.

queries.query: ("LLM" OR "language model" OR "large language model") AND (environment OR simulator OR embodied OR interactive)
queries.rationale: Catches papers studying agents in richer task environments, which often surface architecture ideas transferable to software agents.

plan.coverage_notes: This plan covers the core LLM-agent literature plus distinct practical angles a working engineer would care about: planning, tools, memory, multi-agent coordination, coding agents, evaluation, and reliability. I favored engineering-grounded themes and implementation-relevant architectures over pure alignment theory or highly abstract agent foundations. I also included a few broader recall-safety queries because terminology in this area is inconsistent and many relevant papers avoid the exact phrase 'LLM agent.'
